content.title: About
content.content: Stewed chicken wings are tender pieces of poultry slowly cooked in a flavorful sauce with vegetables and spices. They have a juicy texture, rich taste, and a mild hint of heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stewed wings are common in Asian and Mediterranean cuisines.
Stewing retains more nutrients compared with deep‑frying.
Chicken wings are a popular snack at sporting events and buffets.
Traditional stewing sauces may include tomato paste, soy sauce, honey, and spices.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wings supply niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: They contain iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Stewed wings fit well into low‑carb dietary plans.

items.title: Provides collagen
items.content: Slow cooking releases collagen from bones and skin, beneficial for skin and joints.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the sauce is salty, monitor intake, especially for hypertension.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed wings can be served as a main dish, added to salads, sandwiches, or enjoyed as a snack. Reheat quickly in a microwave or skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag at –18 °C, where they remain good for 2‑3 months.
